title: login() returns True for every caller; the password is never checked
evidence: app/auth.py:[redacted] `password` is not read anywhere in the function. The only branch, on `api_key`, logs a warning and falls through to `return True`. There is no TODO or stub marker. No other file in the payload does the check.
failing_case: login('mallory', 'wrong-password', None) returns True. Any caller that gates access on the return value lets anyone in with any password and no API key.
remediation: Verify the password against a stored salted hash with a constant-time compare, and return False on mismatch or a missing credential. If this is a stub, make it raise NotImplementedError so it cannot ship as an allow-all.

title: CheckoutErrors alert points at the disk-full runbook
evidence: monitoring/alerts.yml:4-8 is the CheckoutErrors alert (summary 'Checkout is failing'). Its runbook_url is the same file as DiskFull at line 16. docs/runbooks/disk-full.md says only 'Check the largest folders.' No checkout runbook exists in docs/runbooks/.
failing_case: Checkout errors page the on-call engineer. They open the linked runbook and get disk-cleanup advice. The checkout outage gets no guidance, which wastes time during a revenue-affecting incident.
remediation: Write docs/runbooks/checkout-errors.md and point CheckoutErrors at it. Add a CI check that every runbook_url resolves to a file, or to a URL that returns 200.

title: web container has a readiness probe but no liveness probe
evidence: deploy/web.yaml:9-14. Only readinessProbe is set. Memory and CPU limits are set, but no requests.
failing_case: The web process deadlocks but stays alive. Readiness fails and traffic stops, but Kubernetes never restarts the container, so the pod stays out of service until someone intervenes by hand.
remediation: Add a livenessProbe on a cheap /healthz endpoint with a sensible initial delay and failure threshold. Set resource requests as well as limits.
